purpose: Four-page visual narrative outline for the journey section; no new data or generated app imagery.

pages.headline: Useful tools already work before contact
pages.subhead: Existing functions set the baseline for a new idea
pages.body:
The desktop walkthrough reached five useful entry journeys: vehicle comparison, finance previews, service-cost guidance, a digital-certificate entry and test-drive scheduling previews. Some paths then ask for a plate or VIN; those downstream steps were not tested.

This changes the starting point for the research. A proposed improvement needs to resolve a specific decision or handoff beyond these existing functions. The observations establish reachable page states, not customer comprehension, completed bookings or incremental sales.
pages.confidence: Observed specific page states; no customer outcome test.

visual.title: What the evaluator could reach
visual.design: Five generous horizontal rows, each with a short task label, observed endpoint and explicit status. This is a research evidence map, not a mock app screen.
visual.annotation: Existing access does not establish successful fulfilment.
avoid: Do not draw five completed-customer checkmarks.
Do not label certificate entry as a certificate actually retrieved.

pages.source_caption: Logged-out desktop observations, 11 November 2026. Evidence UX02-UX05, JX02-JX03 and XT02/XT04/XT06. Safe endpoints only.
pages.boundary: Desktop only. Reaching a page is not a completed customer task or a causal business result.

pages.headline: Insurance timing moves cash between now and later
pages.subhead: The existing calculator already exposes a meaningful tradeoff
pages.body:
Changing only insurance-payment timing reduced the displayed cash needed upfront by Rp45.31 million, while raising the remaining monthly instalment by Rp1.13 million. The car, city, base down payment and first-instalment timing stayed the same.

The existing calculator therefore already answers a useful budget question. A further explanation could help a buyer understand cash at delivery and later payments. Whether that explanation improves a purchase decision remains untested. These are conditional simulator outputs, not binding lender or insurance quotes.
pages.confidence: Observed matched simulator settings; customer comprehension and purchase effect untested.

visual.title: Less cash now comes with larger later instalments
visual.design: Use the same scenario colors and ordering in both panels. Keep separate axes, large direct value labels and readable scenario labels. Do not stack the two financial quantities.
avoid: Do not infer an APR or lender approval.
Do not call disclosed timing a hidden fee.
Do not treat a base DP as the full upfront amount.

pages.headline: A BEV page shows a clear label mismatch
pages.subhead: A specific rendered defect gives the research a sharper target
pages.body:
The selected bZ4X page labels its fuel system as BEV, yet places 7311 under a tank-capacity field measured in litres. The value was visible in both the page and its accessibility tree.

This gives us a precise information-quality issue to investigate. It does not establish the correct engineering value, the underlying cause or whether a customer changed a decision. The useful question is whether specific labels help a buyer understand the relevant vehicle tradeoff.
pages.confidence: Certain about the rendered label/value pair; engineering meaning and customer effect unverified.

visual.title: As displayed for bZ4X A/T
visual.annotation: Translated labels; displayed values unchanged. Research redraw, not a product screenshot.
visual.design: Show two large, clean rows. Emphasize the second label/value pairing with one restrained highlight. Place the exact specification URL and observation date immediately below.
avoid: Do not display 7311 as a validated vehicle capacity.
Do not invent a corrected number, technical diagnosis, failure rate or abandonment effect.
Do not fabricate an app/browser screenshot.

pages.source_caption: Observed selected bZ4X A/T specification, 11 November 2026; XT05/XTS02. Page and accessibility state checked; no engineering validation.
pages.boundary: This is one specific page state. No universal website failure or causal customer effect is inferred.

pages.headline: Preview works; confirmation remains a later step
pages.subhead: Preserved branch context and tentative windows have different meanings
pages.body:
The bZ4X journey exposed Juanda's date and time previews before contact. Its FAQ says staff later confirms the schedule and unit availability. That confirmation was not observed because no request was submitted.

Branch context also survived two tested handoffs: Juanda with bZ4X, then Cempaka Putih with Hiace. The second route changed the preceding branch selection. These counterexamples shift the question toward actual availability and fulfilment. They do not establish a universal handoff problem, a confirmed vehicle or a completed visit.
pages.confidence: Observed preview and preserved context; later confirmation is stated by the FAQ, not observed in operation.

visual.type: request-state diagram with two-row handoff inset
visual.title: Observed access stops before the operational promise
visual.design: Use no more than five short state labels. Label observed, stated and untested states explicitly, with distinct line styles as well as color. The handoff inset supports the baseline; it must not look like a confirmed booking.
avoid: Do not label the calendar as live inventory or a confirmed slot.
Do not turn the five states into an observed conversion funnel.
Do not claim mobile or native-app coverage.

pages.source_caption: Logged-out desktop, 11 November 2026; XT06 and XT08. Juanda date/time preview and booking FAQ; two actual branch links checked after loading.
pages.boundary: Desktop only. Zero mobile-emulated and native-app journeys: local browser launch blocked by socket permissions; native DevTools blocked by organization policy; no available native emulator identified.
